Operation 'step_coverage' has semantic quality issues: vague_summary, missing_output_details. Original summary 'Coverage election' is too generic and doesn't specify what is being elected. data.current_description: One thing: the annual maximum. Do NOT ask how many employees -- that was elected at signup, it is what the membership is billed on, and this endpoint ignores it. Do NOT ask who the plan covers -- it always covers employees and their dependants, dependent_coverage defaults to that, and asking invites an agent to talk somebody out of coverage that costs them nothing. Lead with the recommendation rather than the range: say Denta recommends $1,500 per person and ask whether that is what they want, so somebody with no view can agree in one word; only if they say no offer that anything from $100 to $5,000 works. The response carries the security deposit in cents -- quote it, never compute. The deposit falls due later, before the plan can be used.
data.summary_suggestion: Step 4 of 5: Set annual maximum benefit
data.description_suggestion: Elects the annual maximum benefit per person for the dental plan. The endpoint accepts only the annual_maximum parameter; employee count and coverage scope are fixed from signup and cannot be modified here. Always lead with the Denta recommendation of $1,500 per person; acceptable range is $100-$5,000. Returns the updated plan configuration including the security deposit amount in cents (which must be quoted as-is, not computed). The deposit becomes due before plan activation.
data.reasoning: Original summary 'Coverage election' is too generic and doesn't specify what is being elected. Description is verbose and contains operational guidance mixed with technical details. Improved summary clarifies the specific action (setting annual maximum). Improved description separates technical requirements (what parameters are accepted/ignored) from agent guidance, clearly states inputs and outputs, and explains the security deposit side effect for AI agent clarity.
